newsitem.title: USA: Western Pacific Air sees Q3 loss.
newsitem.headline: Western Pacific Air sees Q3 loss.

text.p: Western Pacific Airlines said on Monday, after the market closed, that it expects to report a third quarter loss in the range of $800,000 to $950,000.

"Western Pacific's operations for the quarter experienced a lower passenger load factor than anticipated, reflecting, among other things, the effect of the adverse publicity from the ValuJet and TWA accidents and aggressive summer capacity and pricing initiatives by competitors at both Colorado Springs and Denver," said Ed Beauvais, chief executive officer.
"We also incurred an escalation in fuel costs resulting from the Persian Gulf activity in Iraq and the 10 percent ticket tax was reimposed in September," he said.
The company said its total operating cost per available seat mile is in the low $0.06 range.
Western Pacific Air said that while it believes that this is the lowest in the industry, it can still do better and is now in an extensive cost review.
The company said while the fourth quarter may be "disappointing" as well, 1997 looks promising.
